question: What is the minimum age required for a citizen of India to have the right to vote in an election? 🗳️
explanation: Awesome! Thanks to Universal Adult Franchise, every Indian citizen who is 18 years of age or older has the equal right to vote and choose their leaders! 🧑
hint: It is the age when a person is officially considered an adult in India.

question: What does the 'F' in UAF stand for in the context of voting? 📜
explanation: Brilliant! UAF stands for Universal Adult Franchise. In civics, 'Franchise' simply means the right to vote in public elections! 🗳️
hint: It sounds like a word used for opening a chain of stores, but here it means voting rights.

question: Which independent body is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India? 🏛️
explanation: Great job! The Election Commission of India (ECI) is a powerful and independent body that manages everything about elections in our country! 🏢
hint: Look for the option that has 'Election' in its name.

question: What is the modern machine used by voters in India to cast their votes? 🖲️
explanation: Fantastic! India uses Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) to record votes quickly, safely, and without wasting paper! 🗳️
hint: The name tells you exactly what it does: it's a machine for voting electronically.

question: What is the list called that contains the names of all the people eligible to vote in an area? 📝
explanation: Spot on! The Electoral Roll, commonly called the Voter List, is prepared before elections to ensure only registered citizens cast their votes! 📜
hint: Think of it as the ultimate 'guest list' for election day.

question: What fundamental principle ensures that a rich person's vote and a poor person's vote have the exact same value? ⚖️
options: One person, one vote, one value 🤝
answer: One person, one vote, one value 🤝
explanation: Excellent! Democracy stands on equality. The rule of 'One person, one vote, one value' means every citizen's voice is equally important! 🤝
hint: It is a rule that repeats the word 'one' three times.

question: Which option on the EVM allows a voter to reject all the candidates running in the election? 🚫
explanation: Superb! NOTA stands for 'None of the Above'. It gives voters the power to say they don't find any of the candidates suitable! 👎
hint: It is an abbreviation for 'None of the Above'.

question: What is the special paper trail attached to EVMs that allows voters to verify their vote called? 🧾
explanation: Awesome! VVPAT stands for Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail. It prints a small slip so you can visually check that your vote went to the right candidate! 🖨️
hint: It starts with two 'V's.

question: What is the official photo identity card issued to voters by the Election Commission called? 🪪
explanation: Perfect! EPIC stands for Elector's Photo Identity Card. It is your official pass to prove your identity at the polling booth! 🪪
hint: It is an epic card to have! It stands for Elector's Photo Identity Card.

question: What geographical area does an elected leader represent in the Parliament or State Assembly? 🗺️
explanation: Great job! The country is divided into different areas for the purpose of elections. Each of these areas is called a constituency! 🗳️
hint: It is a big word starting with 'C' that means an electoral district.

question: What is applied to a voter's finger to prevent them from voting more than once? ☝️
explanation: Spot on! Polling officers apply special indelible ink on the voter's left index finger. It doesn't wash off easily, preventing double voting! 🖋️
hint: It is a dark mark that stays on your skin for days.

question: Who sets the dates and the complete schedule for elections in India? 🗓️
explanation: Fantastic! The Election Commission of India is completely in charge of creating the timetable and setting the dates for elections! 🏢
hint: It's the independent body that manages all things related to voting.

question: What is the process called where citizens vote privately so nobody else knows who they voted for? 🤫
explanation: Awesome! The Secret Ballot system ensures that you can vote without any pressure or fear, keeping your choice completely confidential! 🗳️
hint: It is a combination of the words 'Secret' and 'Ballot'.

question: Before EVMs were introduced, how did voters cast their votes? 📜
explanation: Brilliant! Before machines, people used paper ballots. They stamped their choice on a paper and dropped it into a sealed ballot box! 📦
hint: Think of paper and a container.

question: What helps illiterate voters identify the candidate they want to vote for on an EVM? 🐘
explanation: Excellent! Every party and independent candidate has a unique symbol (like a flower, cycle, or hand). This makes it easy for everyone, even if they can't read, to vote! 🌸
hint: They are pictures like a lotus, a hand, or a bicycle.

question: What is the set of guidelines that political parties must follow during election campaigns called? 📜
explanation: Spot on! The Model Code of Conduct is issued by the Election Commission to make sure political parties campaign fairly and peacefully! ⚖️
hint: It's a 'Model' set of rules for good 'Conduct'.

question: What is the minimum age to contest as a candidate in the Lok Sabha elections? 🧑‍💼
explanation: Great job! While you can vote at 18, you must be at least 25 years old to stand as a candidate for the Lok Sabha! 👔
hint: It's 7 years more than the voting age.

question: What is the term for a candidate who does not belong to any political party? 🚶
explanation: Awesome! An Independent Candidate is someone who fights the election on their own, without the backing of an established political party! 🚶
hint: The word means standing on your own, not dependent on others.

question: Which of these is NOT allowed during election campaigning according to the Model Code of Conduct? 🚫
explanation: Perfect! Bribing voters is illegal and strictly against the Model Code of Conduct. Elections must be fair and based on free will! 💸
hint: Think of an unfair and illegal way to get votes.

question: What is the day called when all the votes are officially tallied and the winner is announced? 📊
explanation: Fantastic! After voting is done, the EVMs are secured, and on Counting Day, the votes are tallied to find out who won the election! 📈
hint: It's the day when numbers are 'counted'.

question: What sound does an EVM make to confirm that your vote has been successfully recorded? 🔊
explanation: Brilliant! When you press the blue button next to your chosen candidate, a red light glows and a long beep sounds to confirm your vote! 📢
hint: It is an electronic noise that lasts for a few seconds.

question: What is the place where people go to cast their votes on election day called? ⛺
explanation: Excellent! The Election Commission sets up Polling Stations (or booths) in schools and community halls so people in that area can vote easily! 🏫
hint: It is a station or a booth set up for polling.

question: Who is the official in charge of a single polling booth on election day? 👮
explanation: Spot on! The Presiding Officer is appointed by the Election Commission to ensure everything runs smoothly and fairly inside that specific polling booth! 👨‍🏫
hint: They 'preside' over the booth.

question: How long is the normal term of a government elected to the Lok Sabha? ⏳
explanation: Awesome! In India, general elections for the Lok Sabha are usually held every 5 years to give citizens a chance to choose their government again! 🗓️
hint: It is half a decade.

question: What are elections called when they are held for the whole country to elect the Lok Sabha? 🇮🇳
explanation: Great job! General Elections are massive events where citizens all over the country vote to elect Members of Parliament (MPs) to form the national government! 🌍
hint: Think of a word that means 'widespread' or 'overall'.

question: If an elected representative resigns or passes away, what kind of election is held just for that one vacant seat? 🪑
explanation: Fantastic! A By-election is a special election held to fill a political office that has become vacant between regularly scheduled elections! 🔄
hint: It starts with the prefix 'By-'.

question: Can a person vote if they are 18 years old but their name is NOT on the Electoral Roll? 🚫
options: Yes, if they talk to the police 👮
explanation: Perfect! Even if you are 18, you must register as a voter. If your name is not on the Electoral Roll, you are not allowed to cast a vote! ❌
hint: Being on the 'guest list' is mandatory.

question: When is National Voters' Day celebrated in India? 🎆
explanation: Brilliant! National Voters' Day is celebrated on 25th January every year to encourage more young voters to take part in the political process! 🗳️
hint: It is exactly one day before Republic Day.

question: What is a document released by a political party explaining its promises and plans if they win? 📖
explanation: Excellent! A Manifesto is a published declaration of the intentions, motives, and views of the political party. It helps voters decide who to vote for! 📜
hint: It starts with an 'M'.

question: In a true democracy, who holds the ultimate power? 👑
explanation: Spot on! The word democracy means 'rule by the people'. The citizens have the ultimate power because they choose their leaders through elections! 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
hint: Abraham Lincoln said democracy is 'of the ______, by the ______, for the ______'.

question: What is the process of putting forward one's name as a candidate for an election called? 📝
explanation: Awesome! Candidates must file their 'Nomination' papers with the election officer to officially declare they are running in the election! ✒️
hint: Think of the word used when a movie is selected for an award.

question: Which of the following is true about Universal Adult Franchise? 🌍
options: All adult citizens can vote without discrimination 🤝
answer: All adult citizens can vote without discrimination 🤝
explanation: Great job! Universal Adult Franchise guarantees that voting rights are given to everyone regardless of their gender, religion, caste, or wealth! 🤝
hint: Look for the option that includes 'All' and 'without discrimination'.

question: Before Independence, did everyone in India have the right to vote? ⏳
options: No, only a privileged few had voting rights 🎩
No, voting didn't exist at all 🚫
answer: No, only a privileged few had voting rights 🎩
explanation: Fantastic! Under British rule, only a tiny percentage of the population (usually the wealthy or highly educated) had the right to vote. Universal Franchise changed that! 🎩
hint: Think about whether the British treated all Indians equally.

question: During elections, why do candidates hold rallies and give speeches? 🎤
options: For Election Campaigning to win votes 📣
answer: For Election Campaigning to win votes 📣
explanation: Perfect! This period is called Election Campaigning. Candidates try to convince voters that their ideas are the best so people will vote for them! 📣
hint: They want to persuade people to choose them.

question: Who provides security at polling booths to make sure voters can vote safely? 👮
explanation: Brilliant! The Election Commission deploys Police and special security forces to ensure that voting happens peacefully and without any bullying! 🛡️
hint: They wear uniforms and maintain law and order.

question: What is a 'Voter Slip' used for? 🎫
options: To buy snacks at the booth 🍪
To know your polling booth and serial number 📍
To write a letter to the Prime Minister ✍️
answer: To know your polling booth and serial number 📍
explanation: Excellent! Political parties and election officials distribute voter slips to help voters easily find their polling booth room and their number on the voter list! 📍
hint: It provides information on where you need to go.

question: What happens if a polling machine (EVM) breaks down during voting? 🛠️
options: The machine is quickly replaced by officials 🔄
The candidate with the most votes so far wins 🏆
answer: The machine is quickly replaced by officials 🔄
explanation: Awesome! Election officials always keep backup EVMs ready. If one malfunctions, they quickly replace it so voting can continue smoothly! 🔄
hint: Think about what a good management team would do.

question: If you move from Delhi to Mumbai permanently, what must you do to vote in Mumbai? ✈️
options: Fly back to Delhi every election 🛩️
Register your name in the Electoral Roll of Mumbai 📝
Show your Delhi ID and vote anywhere 🪪
answer: Register your name in the Electoral Roll of Mumbai 📝
explanation: Spot on! You must update your address and register your name in the Electoral Roll of your new constituency to be able to vote there! 📝
hint: You need to update your details on the official 'guest list' of your new city.

question: What color is the button you press on the EVM next to your chosen candidate's symbol? 🔵
explanation: Great job! On the balloting unit of the EVM, there is a blue button right next to the candidate's name and symbol. You press it to cast your vote! 🔵
hint: It is the color of the sky.

question: How many votes can one citizen cast in a single election? ☝️
explanation: Fantastic! Because of the 'One person, one vote' rule, every citizen is legally allowed to cast only one vote in an election! ☝️
hint: Look at the indelible ink on the finger—it ensures you only go once.

question: What does a government become if it is elected by the people through fair elections? 🏛️
explanation: Perfect! A Democracy is a system of government where the citizens exercise power by voting. India is the largest democracy in the world! 🤝
hint: It starts with a 'D'.

question: Can someone force you to vote for a specific candidate? 😠
options: No, voting is your free and secret choice 🛡️
answer: No, voting is your free and secret choice 🛡️
explanation: Awesome! Nobody can force, threaten, or bribe you to vote for anyone. The secret ballot ensures your choice remains entirely your own! 🛡️
hint: Elections must be 'Free and Fair'.

question: What usually happens 48 hours before the end of voting on election day? 🤫
explanation: Brilliant! To give voters a peaceful time to think, public campaigning, rallies, and speeches must stop 48 hours before voting ends! 🛑
hint: It's a time of silence to help voters think clearly.

question: Who helps visually impaired (blind) citizens to read the EVM? 🦯
explanation: Excellent! EVMs have Braille markings on them to help visually impaired voters easily recognize the buttons and vote independently! 🔢
hint: It is a tactile writing system used by people who are visually impaired.

question: Why is the independence of the Election Commission so important? ⚖️
options: To ensure elections are fair and unbiased 🛡️
So they can become the government 🏛️
answer: To ensure elections are fair and unbiased 🛡️
explanation: Spot on! An independent Election Commission isn't controlled by the ruling party. This ensures that elections are completely free, fair, and honest! 🛡️
hint: Like a referee in a sports match, they must not favor any team.

question: What happens if a candidate gets the highest number of votes in a constituency? 🏆
options: They have to fight a boxing match 🥊
explanation: Great job! In our system, the candidate who secures the most votes in a constituency wins the election and represents the people in the government! 🏛️
hint: They go to the Parliament or Assembly.

question: What does a political party need to form the government in the Lok Sabha? ⚖️
explanation: Fantastic! To form the government, a political party (or a group of parties) must win more than half (a majority) of the total seats in the Lok Sabha! 📈
hint: They need more than 50% of the elected representatives.

question: Is voting currently allowed via smartphones from home during Indian General Elections? 📱
options: No, you must visit a polling booth 🏫
answer: No, you must visit a polling booth 🏫
explanation: Perfect! To keep voting secret and safe from hacking, citizens must physically go to a polling booth to cast their vote on an EVM! 🏫
hint: Think about the security of the secret ballot.

question: What does the word 'Universal' mean in Universal Adult Franchise? 🌍
options: Applying to all adult citizens without exception 🤝
answer: Applying to all adult citizens without exception 🤝
explanation: Awesome! 'Universal' means it covers everybody. Every single adult citizen gets the right to vote, no matter who they are or where they come from! 🤝
hint: It means 'everyone'.

question: Who is the head of the Election Commission of India? 👨‍⚖️
explanation: Brilliant! The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) heads the Election Commission and guides the massive process of conducting elections across India! 🧑‍⚖️
hint: Look for the title that has 'Election' in it.
